steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease two 12-cup muffin pans or line with paper cups.

To make the rhubarb muffins: Stir flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt together in a medium bowl. Beat brown sugar, buttermilk, oil, egg, and vanilla in a separate bowl with an electric mixer until smooth. Pour in dry ingredients and mix by hand just until blended. Stir in rhubarb and chopped walnuts. Spoon batter into the prepared cups, filling almost to the top.
To make the streusel topping: Stir sugar, melted butter, and cinnamon together in a small bowl; sprinkle about 1 teaspoon streusel on top of each muffin.
Bake in the preheated oven until muffin tops spring back when lightly pressed, about 25 minutes. Cool in the pans for 10 minutes, then serve warm or transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Aunt Norma's Rhubarb Muffins
raw_recipe.description: These fabulous rhubarb muffins are moist and sweet, loaded with fresh rhubarb and chopped walnuts, and topped with a crunchy cinnamon-sugar streusel.

review.reviewBody: Read all the reviews and made them just as written except I didn't have buttermilk on hand and couldn't shop, so I put 2 tsp of vinegar in a cup of milk and let it set up. Muffins smelled so fabulous and were delicious. Only drawback was I couldn't stop licking the batter.

I have a ton of rhubarb this spring and am always looking for new recipes in how to use it. After reading a few dozen reviews, I too added 1/4 cup of whole wheat flour instead of entirely all purpose flour. I used plain yogurt in place of the buttermilk and added another 1/2 tsp of baking soda. For the topping, I used 2 tbsp butter and added 1 tbsp flour to make it a bit more crumbly. The cooking time took about 35 minutes. Wow, amazing!!! moist and delicious. However, I only got 18 instead of 2 dozen. I used the large Pampered Chef scoop. Works really well. Next time I will use less sugar in the topping - a bit too sweet for me but OH SO DELICIOUS!!! Thanks for a great recipe 5/19/23 - made a 2nd time - baked as per the recipe exactly this time. I did not add the topping - I forgot it. Oh well - they are still very good.

New favorite! Loved them so much I'm making another batch today since the last one was eaten yesterday. Left out the nuts (personal taste) and followed others' recommendations by adding 1/4 tsp cinnamon to the batter and using 2 cups of rhubarb. I split the batter into only12 cups to make jumbo muffins - they don't rise much - and baked for 30 min. I topped with a traditional streusel rather than just cinnamon-sugar.

Delicious and so easy to make. My changes include adding 1.5 teaspoons cinnamon and 0.5 teaspoon nutmeg and cardamon to the dry ingredients and decreasing the brown sugar to 3\4 c.. I mixed 0.5 cup of the flour into the rhubarb and set it aside, combined the rest of the dry ingredients together in one bowl, and all of the wet ones into another. As with many others, I used milk and lemon juice in place of the buttermilk. After quickly mixing the wet and dry ingredients, I swirled in the rhubarb and flour. I divided the batter between 12 mini loaves and topped them with a double batch of the brown sugar, butter and cinnamon crumble. The muffins took an extra 5 minutes to cook.

Option: Apple and almonds

I used 2 cups of rhubarb, 2 Tbl vanilla, 1 teaspoon of nutmeg, 1 Tbl spoon cinnamon, 1 cup chopped walnuts and fill the cupcakes high , lots of topping and bake for 23 min. Wow. Muffin tops are fantastic and the muffins are sooo good.

Light and fluffy muffins! 
I made a couple of changes to the recipe. I added about 1T sugar to the fresh, real small rhubarb chunks I cut and then microwaved it for three minutes. I drained the rhubarb while I prepared the recipe. I added some fresh lavender since I just found out it goes well with rhubarb. 
For the topping I added a dash of cardamom and a little dried oatmeal that I chopped up. 
The recipe made 24 muffins and they baked in my gas, convection oven for 18 minutes.

I followed the advice of some one the other reveiws and doubled the rhubarb in the recipe. Other than that, I did not change a thing. These are amazing! You get the tart of the rhubarb and the sugary cinnamon in the same bit. They are super moist even a few days later. I made a batch with gluten free flour (substituting equal amounts regular for gluten free, I used Cup4Cup) and I wouldn’t know they were gluten free had I not made them myself! One thing to note, if you glob the cinnamon sugar on top in may form a little crater on the top of your muffin. To avoid that, make sure you are sprinkling the cinnamon sugar evenly over the top of the muffin.

Lovely and moist. I, too, replaced a cup of AP flour with whole wheat and reduced the sugar by a 1/4 cup and increased the rhubarb and I still think I could reduce the sugar some but that might affect the final product. I tried a reviewer’s suggestion of adding a Tbsp of flour to the streusel topping and that gave it more substance. Also used 1/2 white and 1/2 brown sugar in the streusel. Sorry to mess with it Aunt Norma but your basic recipe is a winner!

Love these muffins, although I did add a pinch of cinnamon and nutmeg to the batter. May be my new fav batter - I think these would also taste great with apple, blueberries or raspberries. Going in my "use often" file! I also chose to make 12 large muffins instead of 24, and got pretty great tops. Thank you!

I made it close to recipe except using milk and vinegar and 2 cups rhubarb. Muffins were moist, had a nice flavour and one of the best rhubarb muffins I’ve made yet. It made a nice size 18 muffins. Baked 23 min. I like storing these muffins in fridge. I used -parchment large baking cups.

Great recipe. Made it as written first time but then made some modifications to make it meet my preferences. I upped the rhubarb to 2 cups, cut the brown sugar down to 1 cup and found it to be sweet enough while preserving the tartness of the rhubarb. I've also skipped the topping to reduce the amount of sugar but it is nice to have a crunchy streusel topping. This is a keeper!
As is
I bake a lot, have tons of recipes. Both my husband and myself feel this is the best muffins recipe I’ve ever made. I added a bit more rhubarb and it was perfect. T U.

Delicious, tender and moist. I added a tablespoon of cinnamon to the dry ingredients and substituted in 1/2 cup of coconut sugar with the remaining brown sugar, for extra flavour and lower glycemic index. I placed a tiny doll up of orange marmalade inside the muffins for a surprise!

Thanks to some reviewer suggestions, I added 1 Tbsp cinnamon to the flour mixture, increased BP to 1-1/2 tsp, increased vanilla extract to 2 Tbsp, rhubarb to 2 cups, and walnuts to 1 cup, and also added 1 Tbsp flour to the topping mixture. The final batter was so soupy (not sure what happened?!?) that I added 1 cup of oatmeal to thicken it. Baked for a total of about 30 minutes, and oh my, they baked up beautifully and taste wonderful.
Very bland taste. Add something else like cinnamon or dome sort of other fruit flavoring to batter.

Great recipe! I made a few changes for slightly healthier muffins: used regular milk, 1/4 c less sugar, used palm sugar, and used 1/2 whole wheat flour. I also made 12 in a larger sized muffin tin, and didn't make the sprinkle topping but used course sparkling sugar on top. You never know when you make a few changes if the results are going to be good, but these are great!
Really good! Moist. I substituted just a hint of mini chocolate chips for walnuts as a variation.
This is the first recipe that I made with my new muffin top baking pan. I added about 1/3 cup batter to each cup and baked for 15 minutes. They turned out perfect!
Made as written. Delicious! Might be my go-to rhubarb muffin recipe now.
